gaps.description: The claim does not say why refund-processing data must remain within approved UK-hosted infrastructure. If law, regulation or an external contract imposes the restriction, it would be an external mandate that no project actor may waive, not the project boundary proposed here.

The claim limits refund-processing data to approved UK-hosted infrastructure but does not say which infrastructure is approved or who grants approval, so conformance with the constraint cannot yet be determined.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The claim sets a deadline for completing approved refunds. It governs the result delivered, not how a solution is built, so it is a requirement. A bounded completion window makes refund handling predictable, so it serves the existing refunds goal.
nodes.statement: Refund processing must complete within thirty calendar days after the refund is approved.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The claim removes hosting and data-location options from any refund-processing solution rather than stating what is delivered, so it is a constraint on how the refunds goal may be realised. No supplied evidence shows it is imposed by law, regulation or an external contract, so it is proposed as a project boundary.
nodes.statement: Refund-processing data must remain within approved UK-hosted infrastructure; it may be stored and processed only there.
